issues.detail: The Vietnamese translation renders 'τον παιδα' (the boy) as 'đầy tớ ấy' (that servant/boy). While 'pais' can mean a male child or servant, in the context of Mark 9:17-28, it refers to the child/son. More importantly, the Vietnamese 'đầy tớ' implies a servant status that is not present in the Greek text.
